published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. As restated in TSH gr-qc/9608036 (READ): p.3 'Recent work by Anderson, Hiscock, and Samuel [12] has demonstrated that the DeWitt-Schwinger approximation is quite accurate so long as the radius of curvature of the spacetime is greater than the Compton wavelength of the massive field. In contrast, the various analytic approximations for massless fields are not as robust, and, in all but Ricci flat spacetimes, contain an arbitrary parameter whose value cannot be fixed except by experiment [12].' p.6 'Anderson, Hiscock, and Samuel [19,12] have developed a method and numerical program able to calculate the stress-energy tensor of a quantized scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling and mass in a general static spherically symmetric spacetime. In the course of developing this method, an analytic approximation schemes for calculating the stress-energy tensor for a massive scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling was developed. The approximation developed amounts to an alternate derivation of the DeWitt-Schwinger approximation utilizing a WKB expansion ... In order to obtain the expansion to order 1/m^2 it is necessary to carry the WKB expansion out to sixth order. This approximation ... was found to be exceedingly accurate in Reissner-Nordstrom black hole spacetimes as long as ... mM was greater than unity. For example, choosing Mm = 2 gave fractional accuracy ... of order 10^-2 everywhere outside the event horizon.' p.6 (context): 'Such direct calculations are of course the only way the possible validity of the analytic approximations can be firmly established.' A web-search listing of the abstract (a search-engine summary, not verbatim and not READ) gives: the fields may be massless or massive with arbitrary coupling xi, 'in a zero temperature vacuum state or a nonzero temperature thermal state, and analytical approximations applicable to all these cases are obtained'; numerics in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom spacetimes.
published_hypotheses: (via TSH p.6) Static spherically symmetric spacetime (general), scalar field of arbitrary mass m and curvature coupling xi.

(via TSH p.6) Massive case: WKB expansion carried to sixth order is equivalent to the DeWitt-Schwinger expansion to order 1/m^2. Accuracy is established by comparison with exact numerics in Reissner-Nordstrom black-hole spacetimes for mM > 1; TSH p.13-14 generalise this as 'so long as the mass of the scalar field is large compared with the local radius of curvature'.
(via TSH p.3) Massless case: the analytic approximations are 'not as robust' and, except in Ricci-flat spacetimes, 'contain an arbitrary parameter whose value cannot be fixed except by experiment'.
(via web-search abstract listing, NOT READ) State: zero-temperature vacuum or nonzero-temperature thermal state.

(via the tree's READ of Popov hep-th/0302039, NOT re-read here) Asymptotic flatness: Popov p.1, eq. (70), Sec. VI, as recorded at hpscentre.py:95-99 and :299-301. Per the tree, Popov Sec. IV says the high-frequency part, which is the AHS expression, does not depend on the state; asymptotic flatness enters through the low-frequency part.

(via the tree's READ of AHL gr-qc/9504019, NOT re-read here) The analytic approximation predicts a horizon divergence that the exact numerics do not have (AHL eq. (4), Figs. 3-4; hpscentre.py:126-128).
hypothesis_drift: CANDIDATE, UNRESOLVED (source not read): hpscentre.py:299-301 (DOMAIN_WORD), carried into linstab.py:66-72 and :437-440, says 'the AHS approximation has been derived or established only for asymptotically flat spacetimes (Popov ...)'. TSH p.6 (READ), from AHS's own authors, restates the AHS method as holding 'in a general static spherically symmetric spacetime', with no asymptotic-flatness clause. At p.10-11 TSH apply AHS's DS approximation near a wormhole throat, on the ground that 'our analytic approximate expressions for <T_mu nu> are sufficiently local, only the interior geometry in the neighborhood of the throat is needed'. The 'ESTABLISHED' half of DOMAIN_WORD agrees with TSH: the only tests restated are in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom black-hole spacetimes, which are asymptotically flat. The 'DERIVED' half attributes asymptotic flatness to Popov's derivation, and TSH's restatement of AHS does not carry it. Whether AHS assume asymptotic flatness can only be settled by reading AHS. This is a discrepancy between two restatements, not a refutation, and neither direction favours M. The tree's verdict turns on 'established', and hpscentre.py:108-109 already WITHDREW 'outside the approximation's domain of VALIDITY'.

NONE (massless vs massive carried): HPS take m = 0, xi = 1/6 (qeihps.py:55-59). TSH's accuracy statement ('radius of curvature greater than the Compton wavelength') is for the MASSIVE DS approximation and says nothing about m = 0. The tree does not borrow that accuracy claim; it carries TSH's massless caveat verbatim (hpscentre.py:122-124) and the arbitrary scale mu (qeihps.py:143).

WORDING, not a dropped hypothesis: linstab.py:70-72 and :437-439 ('<T> an APPROXIMATION (AHS), not ... the renormalised <T_ab> of a SPECIFIED state'). Per the web-search abstract listing (not READ) and TSH p.6, AHS approximate <T_ab> IN a specified state: the zero-temperature vacuum or a thermal state. Read as 'an approximation to, not the exact value of, a specified state's <T_ab>', the tree's sentence is accurate. It should not be read as saying the AHS expression belongs to no state. The HPS_STATE_HADAMARD_ESTABLISHED = False flag (qeihps.py:336) records an absence and is not contradicted by anything read.

UNVERIFIABLE CITATION DETAIL: qeihps.py:59-61 cites 'their eq. (4)' for the AHS approximation. From the context this is most likely HPS's eq. (4); hpscentre.py:126-128 separately cites AHL eq. (4). Neither could be checked against AHS. This is recorded, not a finding.

NONE (hedging carried): hpscentre.py:129-132 and :249 (AHS_REACHED = False), qeihps.py:336 and throatmass.py:97 all mark AHS NAMED-NOT-READ / NOT-REACHED and take its hypotheses only from restatements. That matches what this audit could and could not reach.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS. Checked: the AHS DeWitt-Schwinger approximation as TSH gr-qc/9608036 print it (read this run), NOT AHS's own massless formula. C1: TSH (10)-(12) on the zero-tidal Schwarzschild wormhole (Phi = 0, b = r0) are covariantly conserved identically in r and xi (residual 0). C2: from (10)-(12), tension at the throat > 0 iff xi > 23/84, and the exotic condition holds iff xi < 10/84 = 5/42 (exact), so no xi satisfies both, as TSH p.8 state. C3: TSH (15)-(17) on the simple wormhole (b = r0^2/r) are conserved identically (residual 0). C4: the throat roots come out at 0.860358 (tension), with exotic breakpoints 0.151551, 0.2596 and 1.422183; the both-conditions interval is (0.860358, 1.42218) and excludes xi = 0 and xi = 1/6, matching TSH p.9. Everything TSH printed from AHS's DS approximation therefore re-derives. NOT re-derived: AHS's massless (m = 0, xi = 1/6) analytic approximation, which is HPS's source term. AHS was not read. The tree's two transcriptions of that formula (HPS (5)-(7) and Popov (B1)-(B3)) and their conservation repair (16 -> 116 and the dimension repair) are hpscentre.py's own controls (python3 hpscentre.py --selftest, about 2 min). They are not repeated here, because they check HPS's and Popov's printings, not AHS's.

They apply AHS's DS approximation to order 1/m^2 in five wormhole spacetimes, arguing from its locality (p.10-11), and restate its accuracy criterion and its massless arbitrary-parameter caveat. Their printed expressions are conserved and reproduce their thresholds (rederive C1-C4).

lacked_data: What the authors lacked in 1995, and what the restatements show: (a) an experimental value for the massless approximation's arbitrary parameter, which TSH p.3 say 'cannot be fixed except by experiment'. It is still unfixed today, and there is no known fundamental massless conformal scalar to measure it on. (b) Exact numerical <T_ab> outside black-hole spacetimes, against which to test the massless approximation: in non-asymptotically-flat geometries, at regular centres, at wormhole throats. Nothing read here supplies it (the later work surfaced by search was not readable). Would the data change the conclusion? The tree's conclusions that rest on AHS are all of the 'not established' kind: an approximation rather than an exact renormalised <T_ab> in a specified state, a Hadamard state not established, and m < 0 solutions outside the domain where the approximation has been established. (a) would select one member of a family whose mu-dependence is conserved and traceless on its own (qeihps.py:143), so it moves none of them. (b) would not correct AHS; an exact <T_ab> on an m < 0 geometry would REPLACE the approximation and answer O5 directly, which is what the tree already names as its answer (hpscentre.O5_ANSWERED_BY). Evidence on whether AHS is inaccurate: its DS expressions, as its authors print them, are exactly conserved and reproduce their stated thresholds (rederive C1-C4). The one known defect, a spurious horizon divergence (AHL, per the tree), was found and published by the same authors in 1995, so it is a limitation named at the time and not a result later data overturned. No evidence was found that missing data make AHS wrong. Nor can AHS be shown right here, because it was not read.
grade_evidence: The source, PRD 51 4337, has no arXiv copy found and every route to it was blocked: APS, INSPIRE, arXiv, PubMed and academia.edu are egress-blocked, and the alphaXiv quota ran out after one call. So its statement and hypotheses are NAMED-NOT-READ, as the tree itself records (hpscentre.py:129-132, AHS_REACHED = False). Checked here: (1) TSH gr-qc/9608036, same authors, READ. It confirms the tree's central use: AHS gives analytic APPROXIMATIONS, the massive one established by comparison with exact numerics only in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom black-hole spacetimes, and the massless one carrying an arbitrary parameter. (2) The AHS DS expressions TSH print re-derive: conserved identically, thresholds reproduced exactly (sympy, ALL PASS). Not checkable here: whether AHS's DERIVATION assumes asymptotic flatness. The tree says it does (via Popov), while TSH restate AHS as a method for 'a general static spherically symmetric spacetime'. That is recorded as an unresolved discrepancy between restatements, not a narrowing. Also not checkable: AHS's massless formula itself. STANDS would require reading AHS. NARROWED or WRONG would require a shown defect, and none was found. The tree's own statements are appropriately hedged: they claim absence of establishment, not invalidity.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading AHS PRD 51 4337 (APS, or a library scan). Specifically: (i) whether the derivation assumes asymptotic flatness, or only a static spherically symmetric metric plus a vacuum or thermal state, which would decide the 'derived' half of hpscentre.DOMAIN_WORD; (ii) the massless xi = 1/6 approximation as printed, checked against HPS (5)-(7) and Popov (B1)-(B3), including the 16 vs 116 coefficient and the mu term; (iii) the stated domain where accuracy was established. If AHS assume asymptotic flatness and print a formula matching the conserved reading, the grade becomes STANDS. If the derivation holds for general static spherically symmetric spacetimes, the grade becomes STANDS for 'established', and the 'derived' half of DOMAIN_WORD would be recorded as narrower than the source, which is not in M's favour either way since the verdict rests on 'established'. A published exact <T_ab> on a non-asymptotically-flat or regular-centre geometry that disagrees with the approximation would make it NARROWED.
